stored.feedback: Pri logickom závere je bežnejšie „must“ ako „has to“.

examples.reference_before: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
examples.reference_after: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
v_before: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
The director said the office scene would be filmed before lunch.
v_after: The director said they would film the office scene before lunch.
examples.reason: Slovak is active with an explicit subject (oni natocia); the variant turns it into an agentless passive.

examples.reference_before: She never shares food, so this one must be special.
examples.reference_after: She never shares food, so this croissant must be special.
v_before: She never shares food, so this one must be special.
v_after: She never shares food, so this croissant must be special.
examples.reason: Omits the noun 'croissant' (tento croissant), leaving the referent unexpressed.

examples.reference_before: Her trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
examples.reference_after: The trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
v_before: Her trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
v_after: The trainer wishes his pads were a bit thicker.
examples.reason: Adds a possessor 'her' that the Slovak 'Trener' does not have.

examples.reference_before: She had her boots dyed purple last summer.
examples.reference_after: She had her boots dyed purple last year.
v_before: She had her boots dyed purple last summer.
Last summer she had her boots dyed purple.
She got her boots dyed purple last summer.
v_after: She had her boots dyed purple last year.
Last year she had her boots dyed purple.
She got her boots dyed purple last year.
examples.reason: 'Vlani' means last year, not last summer; the time adverbial is wrong in all three variants.

examples.reference_before: Right now he is holding a blue ice pack against the lump.
examples.reference_after: Right now he is pressing a blue ice pack against the lump.
v_before: Right now he is holding a blue ice pack against the lump.
Right now he is pressing a blue ice pack against the lump.
He is pressing a blue ice pack against the lump right now.
v_after: He is pressing a blue ice pack against the lump right now.
examples.reason: 'tlaci' means presses/pushes; 'holding' drops the pressing action and the correct 'pressing' variants are already stored.

examples.reference_before: She usually stays dry, but today she is dancing in the rain.
examples.reference_after: She usually stays under the roof, but today she is dancing in the rain.
v_before: She usually stays dry, but today she is dancing in the rain.
v_after: She usually stays under the roof, but today she is dancing in the rain.
examples.reason: 'ostava pod strechou' states staying under the roof; 'stays dry' replaces the stated content with an inference.

examples.reference_before: You can hear his huge sneeze across the whole meadow.
examples.reference_after: You can hear his huge sneeze across the whole meadow.
v_before: You can hear his huge sneeze across the whole meadow.
His huge sneeze can be heard across the whole meadow.
v_after: You can hear his huge sneeze across the whole meadow.
examples.reason: Slovak fixes an active clause with the explicit subject 'ty mozes pocut'; the variant is passive and drops the hearer.

examples.reference_before: The children awake at seven in the morning.
examples.reference_after: The children will wake up at seven in the morning.
v_before: The children awake at seven in the morning.
v_after: The children will wake up at seven in the morning.
examples.reason: Perfective 'zobudia sa' is future, not present, and the literary verb 'awake' is the wrong register.
